instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires semiannual expense statements filed by principals (not lobbyists), and lobbyists only supply information to the principal for the principal’s filing, so there is no separate annual lobbyist spending report.
Expense statements are due January 31 and July 31 from principals, with lobbyists providing information to principals, so lobbyists are not required to file monthly spending reports.
The only periodic spending/expense statement obligation in the text is imposed on registered principals, not on lobbyists as separate filers, so no other lobbyist-specific cadence applies.
Principals file semiannual expense statements and lobbyists merely provide supporting information, so the statute does not require lobbyists to file quarterly spending reports.
The statute assigns the periodic expense statement filing duty to every registered principal, not to lobbyists, so there is no separate semiannual lobbyist spending report.
Reporting periods are defined as 6-month periods and principals file by Jan. 31 and July 31, with no triannual lobbyist filing requirement.
Itemization requirements in § 13.68 apply to the principal’s expense statement, not to a separate lobbyist-filed spending report, so lobbyists are not required as named filers to itemize expenses.
The statute requires expense statements from principals, while lobbyists only provide information that principals file, so lobbyists have no separate required spending report cadence.
Disclosure of legislative proposals/topics is required from the principal as a condition of lobbying/authorization, not from lobbyists via a separate lobbyist activity/spending report.

Compensation to lobbyists is reported within the principal’s expense statement aggregate totals, but the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to disclose their earnings in a separate lobbyist spending report.

The law requires principals to keep a daily itemization of time spent meeting with officials and related activities, but it does not require lobbyists to disclose contacts in a separate lobbyist-filed report.
Per-issue time proportions are reported by principals (for topics accounting for 10% or more of time), not by lobbyists via a separate spending report.
Issues/topics of lobbying must be reported by the principal to the commission, and the statute does not create a separate lobbyist-filed spending report requiring issue disclosure.
General subjects/topics are reported by principals under § 13.67(1), not by lobbyists as named filers of a separate report.

The expense-statement disclosure components listed in § 13.68 are imposed on principals, and there is no separate lobbyist spending report requiring disclosure of gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging by a lobbyist as filer.
Indirect lobbying costs (e.g., preparation, research, advertising) are reported in the principal’s aggregate totals, but lobbyists are not required as separate filers to disclose such costs.

Wisconsin places periodic spending disclosure obligations on principals’ expense statements and only requires lobbyists to provide information to the principal, so lobbyists are not required to file itemized spending reports.

Although license applications may include a residence address, the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose address/phone number in a separate periodic spending report because no such lobbyist report is required.
Legislative proposals/topics must be reported by the principal, and the statute does not require lobbyists to report bills/actions (or positions) in a separate lobbyist activity report.
Information about the principal’s business activity/nature is required in the principal’s registration statement, not disclosed by lobbyists in a separate lobbyist spending report.

Principal registration requires the principal’s name and business address, but the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose principals’ address/phone number in a separate lobbyist spending report (no such report exists).

Lobbyist authorizations are filed for each principal, but this is not a lobbyist periodic spending report and the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose all principals represented in a separate spending report.
Identification of legislative proposals and proposed administrative rule numbers is reported by the principal to the commission, not by lobbyists as named filers of a separate report.

Direct lobbying costs including compensation to lobbyists are disclosed in the principal’s expense statement, but the statute does not require a separate lobbyist-filed spending report disclosing compensation.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported by the registered principal in its expense statement, and there is no lobbyist-filed periodic spending report requiring totals.

Because periodic spending reports are filed by principals (with lobbyists supplying information), the statute does not impose an itemized spending-report obligation on lobbyists that would satisfy this criterion.
The statute imposes periodic expense statement filing on principals regardless of expenditures, but it does not require lobbyists to file any separate 'no activity' report.

Reporting under § 13.68 covers principals’ aggregate lobbying expenditures rather than a lobbyist’s itemized spending on household members of public officials, and no separate lobbyist spending report exists requiring such disclosure.

Any itemization in § 13.68 pertains to the principal’s expense statement (e.g., daily time itemization), and the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose spending in an itemized format via a separate lobbyist report.
